A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same preconditioned-SGD research. Their main text, equations, figures, notation table, and theoretical and experimental appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original quadratic diagnostics, Fashion-MNIST experiments, and SciML regression, PINN, and Green’s-function evaluations, including repeated-run summaries in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quadratic and SciML experiments and adds empirical measurements of curvature and gradient-noise reduction.

M1.justification: The preconditioned SGD update, neural architectures, and CG-Hessian/CG-GGN procedures are retained. The expanded natural-gradient discussion and new diagnostic do not introduce an optimizer component.

E1.justification: The Fashion-MNIST MLP experiment and its appendix coverage are removed. The quadratic diagnostic, noisy Franke regression, Poisson PINN, and diffusion/convection-diffusion Green’s-function tasks remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding SciML comparisons retain SGD, SGD with momentum, Adam, L-BFGS, CG-Hessian, and CG-GGN. The quadratic deflation variants are also unchanged; newly cited methods are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 changes the reported CG-GGN learning-rate grid from {0.1, 0.05, ..., 0.0001} to {1.0, 0.5, ..., 0.001}, without establishing that experiments were rerun. The added diagnostic examines Phase-II epoch 250 and uses 100 mini-batches. Relative-loss normalization is newly explained, but already appears in v1’s plots.

E4.justification: v2 adds a snapshot analysis of smoothness and gradient-noise reduction on the PINN and two Green’s-function problems, testing the proposed mechanism. It removes the Fashion-MNIST learning-rate sensitivity study in v1 Figure 7. Quadratic deflation analyses and Green’s-function operator checks remain.

E5.justification: The retained experiments still use 30-run quadratic averages and five-run SciML summaries with the same seed ranges and variance bands. The new diagnostic specifies seed 42 and estimates gradient covariance using 100 independent mini-batches, without reporting uncertainty intervals for its reduction factors.

E6.justification: v2 Section 4.5 newly reports L reductions of 78x, 3710x, and 1923x, and noise-trace reductions of 12x, 1505x, and 203x, for the PINN, Laplacian Green’s function, and convection-diffusion Green’s function, respectively. These are snapshot diagnostics. Retained SciML plot images are unchanged; Fashion-MNIST results are removed.

T1.justification: v1 Theorems 4–5 assume almost-sure one-step containment and claim infinite-horizon survival. v2 Theorems 3.5–3.6 replace these with finite-horizon statements, controlled overshoot, additional moment assumptions conditional on survival, and exit bounds containing accumulated noise and overshoot terms. Lemma 3.4 and substantially rewritten appendix proofs support this revised framework.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions narrow the central basin-stability guarantee to survival up to a time horizon, replacing v1’s unrestricted survival claim. This materially changes a principal contribution, while retaining the conditioning/noise-floor design principle and the emphasis on analysis rather than a new optimizer.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes training-loss optimization from generalization, limits the theory to a fixed metric, and qualifies optimizer rankings by the shared Adam warm start. It explains accumulated overshoot risk and interprets the new L/K measurements while treating the PL constant as unchanged. Most existing experimental interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents relative-loss normalization and the new diagnostic’s checkpoint, seed, and first-batch preconditioner construction. It removes the explicit Phase-I Adam learning rate of 0.001 and the Fashion-MNIST implementation details. Software versions, hardware, retained architectures, and CG iteration budgets remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Amari (1998), Amari et al. (2021), Ishikawa and Karakida (2024), and Zhang et al. (2025), expanding discussion of natural gradients, generalization, and structured preconditioning. Kaplan et al. (2020) and Swersky et al. (2011) are removed. The main related-work argument remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially recast, moving the optimizer overview and update equation earlier, and the local-theory exposition is extensively rewritten. Numbered sections, subsections, and Appendices A–D replace unnumbered headings and repair many blank cross-references. The title and front matter also change.

P2.justification: The paper adopts a substantially different TMLR layout, including a redesigned title/author page, typography, headers, margins, and figure placement. v1 Figures 1 and 7 are removed. The quadratic figure adopts common vertical scaling and revised mathematical labeling; retained SciML graphics are reused with edited captions and numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 adds quantitative L/K evidence where v1 offered mainly qualitative SciML explanations and states applicability limits more clearly. These improve support and transparency. The gain is limited by the removed sensitivity study and warm-start learning-rate disclosure, and by a remaining proof gap: Appendix C.2.4 derives Eq. (27) by treating the future no-overshoot event as F_k-measurable, which the stated assumptions do not justify.
